mission.title: Shimada
mission.description: Intercept the renegade redpills who dress like Neo and Trinity, and find out who leads them.

npc.say: Piece of advice, friend: don't think about pulling the wool over Shimada's eyes. She's nobody's fool.
Neo and Trinity are watching over you, whether you realize it or not.
You heard Shimada; hit the road.
What she told you is for you alone.

phase.briefing:
Warrior, we may have a serious problem on our hands. After your recent run-ins with fanatic redpills dressed as Neo and Trinity, we began combing city records for reports of similar encounters. We found a surprising number of reports of similarly dressed people, often involved in fights with groups matching the general description of Cypherites.
Furthermore, a number of hovercraft that left Zion recently have failed to make their scheduled status broadcasts back to Zion Control. Commander Lock believes that the new costumed redpill group is operating from these renegade hovercraft. Most of the data on their crews was somehow wiped from Zion's databases. Fortunately, we happened to have a backup of one crew's data on a portable drive that they seem not to have known about. We've used this data to trace the crew's RSI signals. Intercept the renegades and attempt to subdue them.

enter.say: I've got redpill activity in there.
Looks like the only way you're gonna be able to subdue those nuts is by doing to them what they did to those Cypherites...

objective.text: Kill the E Pluribus Neo Crusader

done.say: Code says there's something on that one. See what they've got.

objective.text: Get the operating orders from the E Pluribus Neo Crusader

done.say: Ah, operating orders: just what a well-trained Zion operative is not supposed to carry with them when they go out in the field. These renegades must be slightly disorganized right now. Head outside while I punch up the coordinates in those orders.

phase.briefing: Good work, {player}! It's unfortunate that the renegades resisted you so violently, but if their aggressive behavior is a symptom of disorganization, then we may be able to disrupt their operations and win them back to Zion while their chain of command is still unsteady.

enter.say: Looks like those orders you captured were legit; I've got more redpill activity in there. Ready for another round of the old "intercept and subdue," i.e. "kick ass, then ask questions later"?
I'm reading an active computer system in that room. It's running some kind of security protocol, though.

done.say: You just hacked the heck out of that thing. My scan shows that you have free access to that computer now.

"Shimada"? Sounds like the name of whoever's directing these people. This could be important. See if you can get a data log of network connections from that computer. Maybe we can use it to track down the guy who was chatting on there: "Cordoba."

objective.text: Get the Data from the computer

done.say: Great. Upload that data to me at a hardline.

objective.text: Upload the data at a hardline

phase.briefing: "Shimada"? The name sounds familiar, {player}. She's probably a Zionite; I'll see what I can dig up. Meanwhile, we've been able to use the network connection data you retrieved to trace the location of Cordoba's terminal. Proceed to his location and see if he's willing to talk about Shimada.

enter.say: I've got more redpill signals in there. Hopefully, Cordoba is one of them. Maybe if we mention Shimada's name they'll be willing to talk.

talk.say:
You want to meet Shimada, huh? Either you've got Neo in your heart, or you're trying to spy on us for that do-nothing Commander Lock. Anyway, you'll get what you deserve from Shimada.
Take Pax and Chang here with you. They'll tell your operator where you need to go.

done.say: That seemed to go well. Guess you'd better head outside with your little escort party.

talk.say: I can't wait to see what Shimada thinks of you. Are you sure you don't want to, you know, put on some decent clothes first?

objective.text: Lead Pax and Chang out of the area

phase.briefing:
Shimada was indeed a Zionite, and responses to my inquiries around Zion indicate that she was in the crew of one of the hovercraft that have missed their last scheduled status broadcast to Zion Control.
Talk to her, {player}, and if you can't persuade her to return the missing hovercraft to Zion, at least try to find out what her group's goals are. Maybe we can still resolve this peaceably.

enter.say: Lots of redpill signals in there. Looks like this Shimada has plenty of security.

talk.say:
You came here seeking answers, operative, but you must find some of them for yourself. I will tell you that our group, E Pluribus Neo, is dedicated to following the teachings and ideals of Neo: most importantly, that all humans should be given the chance of freedom from the Matrix, just as every bird should have a chance to use its wings.
When you understand the truth of that statement, you will be ready to know more. At present, I must ask you to leave. Do not bother trying to call in other operatives for backup; we will be long gone before they can arrive.

mission.finish:
Oh dear. I was afraid of this, Warrior: another schism within Zion. Shimada sounds like a calm, reasonable woman, but her youthful idealism needs tempering with the wisdom of experience.
It's clear from her own words that Shimada is concealing something about her "E Pluribus Neo" group from us. We need to find out what she's hiding. It could be the key to clearing up this misunderstanding, and getting those people back into Zion. If E Pluribus Neo begins waking bluepills at an accelerated rate, the Machines might feel that their power is threatened, and accuse us of aiding a violation of the Truce. And if the Truce fails...
Let us pray that it doesn't come to that.
